pairs.difference: A (campfire): the whole card is pulled to orange. The tent, dirt ground, logs and kettle all share one orange-brown mass, and the stones and pine shadows go flat olive-grey (warm share 0.75, above the real range; shadow chroma kept 0.41, below it). B (viewing binoculars): a cool blue-grey metal subject against pale blue city towers. Its shadows stay a rich deeper blue, as on the real telescope and fan cards.
pairs.fix: Keep the ground a muted grey-brown, make the stones cool blue-grey with blue-violet shadows, keep the sky and pines clearly blue-green, and use orange only in the fire itself.

pairs.difference: A: a yellow-orange player against violet rings, with white earbuds. This is a clear complementary hero and background, like the real juice-on-purple card. B: a nearly colorless silver harmonica (subject chroma 0.049, below the real range) on a loud magenta-purple gradient. The hero has almost no local color and the background does all the work. Both backgrounds are louder than the real cards, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Give the harmonica a cool blue-silver body with visible blue-violet tint in its shadows and warm brass screws, and calm the purple background slightly so the subject reads first.

pairs.difference: A: the cowboy hat is one saturated orange-brown mass whose shadows stay orange-red, with no cooler shift, on a light, loud cyan ray background. This matches the generated glove lessons, while the real glove's shadows go purple-brown. B: a cream and orange jacket with a green sash on green rays. It has more hue families and its shadows are brown. Both are in range, so confidence is low.
pairs.fix: Make the hat a less orange, natural tan-brown felt, let its underside and crease shadows turn toward plum-brown, and use a deeper blue background instead of bright cyan.

pairs.difference: B (pig and farmer by the saloon): almost the whole card is orange. The wood building, dirt, pig, hat and skin all fall into one warm mass (warm share 0.87, far above the real maximum of 0.57). Only the blue shirt breaks it, and there are just 3.4 hue families against 5.2 or more on the real cards. A (festival): violet sky, multicolor stage lights, a pink pig and a white cow give a spread of hues with cool, related shadows.
pairs.fix: Keep the building and ground a muted grey-brown with blue-violet shadows, add a clear blue sky and some green plants, keep the pig pink rather than orange, and limit orange to small accents.

pairs.difference: A (fruit plate): the table is one orange-tan field, and the plate and shadows go khaki-olive in the lens. The fruit is very loud (subject chroma 0.17, above the real range) against a muted background (0.094, below the range), and the whole card leans warm. B (seahorse): an orange hero on a deep blue water gradient, with shadows that move toward plum. This is a clean warm-on-cool hero and background split, like the real cards.
pairs.fix: Paint the table a cooler, greyer wood, make the glass plate and its cast shadow bluish, and bring the fruit down slightly from pure neon red and orange.

pairs.difference: A (cactus): a smooth pink gradient background, a lime-green cactus, and a cast shadow that turns muddy grey-olive on the pink. There are only 1.9 hue families, below the real range, and the subject chroma is above the range. B (vending machine): a blue cabinet on purple, with shadows that stay rich violet and colorful cans inside, which keeps more hue families.
pairs.fix: Make the cactus a natural sage-to-deep green, let its cast shadow on the pink floor turn a deeper rose-violet instead of grey, and add a second accent color such as a magenta or white flower and a terracotta pot.

pairs.difference: B (saloon door): wall, floor, door frame and swinging doors are all orange-brown wood, so the card is nearly monochrome warm (warm share 0.92, above the real maximum; 2.2 hue families). The sky in the doorway reads as grey-green in the lens. A (garden gate): red brick, a blue sky, green trees and grass, and a pink-cream path give several balanced hue families.
pairs.fix: Make the wall planks a weathered grey-brown with cool blue-grey shadows, show a bright blue sky and green bushes through the doorway, and keep the red trim as the single warm accent.

pairs.difference: A (covered wagon): the canvas is a warm cream instead of a cool white, the wood and dirt ground are the same orange, and the shadows are red-brown. This is the same push toward cream neutrals seen in the generated computer lessons. B (popcorn cart): red and white stripes with cool white, a blue background, and grey-lavender paving that rests the eye.
pairs.fix: Make the wagon canvas a clean cool white with blue-grey folds, keep the ground a muted grey-tan, and let the shadows under the wagon go cool brown-violet.

pairs.difference: A (horseshoe): the hero is almost colorless steel (subject chroma 0.034, far below the real minimum of 0.071) on an all-orange wood table. There are only 1.65 hue families and warm share is 0.91, above the real range. B (map and magnifier): blue sea, cream land, a green island and a red compass rose give 5 hue families with a cool-against-warm split.
pairs.fix: Give the horseshoe a cool blue-steel tint with blue-violet shadow sides, make the table a darker, greyer brown, and add one more color such as a green ribbon or a red tag.

pairs.difference: A (neckerchief): the cloth is pushed to pure saturated red with dark-red shadows (subject chroma 0.22, above the real maximum of 0.19), and the badge adds more orange. B (lasso): the rope keeps a natural tan, the red bandana is a small accent, and the cyan background carries the cool side.
pairs.fix: Make the neckerchief a slightly deeper, less neon red, let its folds go toward crimson-plum instead of pure dark red, and keep the badge gold.

pairs.difference: B (towel): a very loud green checker background (chroma 0.22, above the real maximum of 0.15) against a loud orange and yellow towel, with nothing neutral to rest the eye and only 2.6 hue families. A (target booth): also very warm with orange wood, a red panel and an orange bear, but it has a blue and white target and teal walls that break up the warmth.
pairs.fix: Calm the background to a softer mid-green or blue, give the towel a white stripe between the orange and yellow ones, and let its folds shade toward a cooler red-violet.

pairs.difference: A (boxing gloves): the gloves are pushed to pure red (subject chroma 0.18, above the real range), the highlights go orange, and the floor wood is the same orange. B (boots): orange-brown leather on a purple striped background, with shadows that shift toward purple in the lens. These are rich, related shadow colors, like the real glove lesson.
pairs.fix: Make the gloves a deeper, less pure red with soft white highlights instead of orange ones, let their shadows on the floor turn plum, and make the floor a lighter, less orange wood.

pattern: Generated cards pull everything toward one warm orange mass. Wood, dirt, skin and leather all share the same orange, and neutrals are pushed toward cream where the real cards keep them cool white or blue-grey. Shadows either stay the same hue, only darker (orange to red-brown), or go muddy olive-grey, instead of shifting to the rich plum, violet or blue seen on the real cards. Heroes are either pure-hue neon or nearly colorless, with too few hue families, and there is no cool counter-mass to rest the eye.
